pool.text: First Dutch trading post founded by Nicolaes Baliestel and Dirck Claeszoon van Sanen.
French post established near present‑day Paramaribo.
English settlers arrive to found Surinam after earlier settlements abandoned.
Governor Willoughby granted Paramaribo and surrounding lands by King Charles II.
Village of Paramaribo expanded and outranked earlier settlement of Torarica.
Paramaribo conquered by Abraham Crijnssen's squadron during Second Anglo‑Dutch War.
Treaty of Breda confirms Paramaribo as leading town of Dutch Suriname.
Devastating fire in January destroys over 400 buildings in old town.
September fire destroys nearly 50 buildings in old town.
Enslaved people in Suriname legally freed.
Formerly enslaved people allowed to leave sugar plantations, boosting town population.
Paramaribo Zoo opens to public in May.
Paramaribo remains capital after Suriname gains independence.
City divided into 12 administrative resorts during reorganization.
Historic inner city of Paramaribo designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Paramaribo's population reaches roughly 252,581 people, nearly half of Suriname.
